items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: I remember him well, that's my buddy. I used to pitch hit for him with the eagle.

ctx.x: Do you remember Danny Lewis? Danny Lewis?

I remember him well, that's my buddy. I used to pitch hit for him with the eagle. Yeah. He hit there, and Danny Lewis hit John and the Dots of the Island. We'd draw the pitch in there and say, we used to do what I always say, you see. Yeah. And we used to get behind them, you know, when they'd run, and say, da da da da da. Yeah. You know? So, what's that? Old Frankie Dukeson died, and old Danny Lewis cried. And Edward Barton put it aside. He could print good, he could draw good. He'd draw the side, and put all…
He was playing with Frankie Dukeson.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: I'd slip in them dances, you know, like the Oddfellas Hall and I'd play for Danny Lewis, you know.

ctx.x: A little fish fry or a house party? No, no, no, no. For a lawn party or anything? No, some people give a dance. Young kids, you know. They hired a band. You know. And Bruce said, I'm going to take you on the job tonight. Well, you see, 9 o'clock I had to be home. I had to be inside. Go to bed. And when that 9 o'clock come up, you know, that was it. He had me on that job. 9 o'clock come up again and get the drivers in. Sand make up. You know. I said, John, I can't. I'm sleepy. I can't play no more. I'm sleepy, you…
Did you get any, belonged to any regular band then pretty soon? Oh yeah.

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: And I'd watch them. I've got a good ear, you know.

ctx.x: I'd go around different places like I'd go around where the Eagle Band was playing. Danny Lewis would be playing, you know.
